To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thyme oil emulsion stabilized by ovalbumic/gum arabic complexes showed a long-term stability and an excellent antimicrobial activity.
the thyme oil emulsion with OVA-GA bilayers or OVA/GA complex emulsions showed improved physical and antimicrobial stability compared to the thyme oil alone.
the physical properties and the antimicrobial activity of TO emulsions stabilized with OVA/GA bilayer and complexes were significantly influenced by pH and oil phase compositions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of TO emulsions stabilized with OVA and GA.
the development of novel biopolymer stabilized emulsions with improved physical properties and antimicrobials.

the preparation of thyme oil-in-water emulsion stabilized by OVA and GA, and the influence of the interfacial structure on the physical properties, antimicrobial activities and stability of emulsion was studied.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emulsions stabilized with biopolymer (OVA/GA complexes) were able to protect the TO and enhance its antimicrobial activity.
the OVA-GA bilayers and the complexes emulsions were able to provide a long-term stability for the emulsified TO.
the emulsion stabilized by OVA/GA bilayer and complexes had a good potential for application as a natural preservative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OVA/GA bilayer emulsion was more stable and showed higher antibacterial activity compared to the complexes emulsion.
the emulsification process is a useful tool to increase the antimicrobial activity of TO.
thyme oil emulsion stabilized by biopolymers (OVA and/or GA) can be used as an effective antimicrobial system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of biopolymers can be a useful strategy to develop a stable and effective antimicrobial system for essential oils.
the use of biopolymers to stabilize emulsion can be a promising alternative for food and pharmaceutical applications.
the emulsions stabilized with biopolymers (OVA and GA) can be used as an antimicrobial delivery system for essential oils.
